You are given observations of a 3D structure made of unit blocks on a fixed 3×3 grid
    (3 rows and 3 columns; 9 positions total).
    Each observation shows a view of the structure from a specific angle.
    The maximum height of the structure is 3 layers.

    Observations (Top View — a 3×3 matrix; each cell is 1 if ANY layer has a block at that position):
    Top view:
0 0 0
1 0 0
0 0 0

    Task:
    Infer one complete 3D structure that could produce these observations.
    For each Top View cell containing 1, choose a column height of 1, 2, or 3.
    Build that column continuously from Layer 1 up to the chosen height.
    A Top View cell containing 0 must remain empty at every height.

    Structure specifications:
    - Grid: fixed 3×3 (every layer has exactly 3 rows and 3 columns)
    - Maximum height: at most 3 layers, not necessarily exactly 3 layers
    - Each layer is a 3×3 grid with 0 (empty) or 1 (block), stacked from bottom to top

    Important constraints:
    1. Layer 1 is the BOTTOM layer (ground level) — it should contain blocks, not be all zeros
    2. Blocks must be supported from below (a block at height h requires a block at height h-1 in the same position)
    3. The cell-wise OR of all output layers must exactly equal the observed Top View
    4. Do not add unnecessary empty layers at the bottom or top
    5. Layers are numbered from bottom (Layer 1) to top (Layer N)
    6. Do not exceed 3 layers in height
    7. Every layer must be exactly 3 rows × 3 columns — do not use a different grid size

    Required output skeleton (replace each row description with three binary digits):
    Reasoning:
    Briefly state the chosen heights and check the support and Top View constraints.
    Structure:
    Layer 1:
    <bottom row 1>
    <bottom row 2>
    <bottom row 3>

    The skeleton shows one layer. Continue with Layer 2 and then Layer 3 in the same format
    only when the chosen heights require them. Never include an all-zero layer.

    Formatting rules:
    1) Begin with one brief Reasoning: section, then output exactly one Structure block
    2) Each layer has exactly 3 rows of 3 digits
    3) Do not start with an empty bottom layer
    4) Do not add unsupported floating blocks
    5) Do not exceed 3 layers in height
    6) Do not output row descriptions or angle brackets; output only 0 and 1 in each grid row
    7) Do not write a second Structure block or anything after the final grid row
